$doc: Planner choices that are data, not code (PHASE2-PLAN principle: craft lives in code, choices live in data). Every number cites its source; 'planner default' marks a value the plan leaves open, which the owner may overrule (docs/OWNER-DECISIONS.md). Loaded and checked by planner/policy.mjs.

sampling.$doc: How the planner weighs legal options before the hard rules (G-SPEC) filter them.

uniqueness.$doc: Exact fingerprint never reused; structural distance against the channel's last 14 days (PHASE2-PLAN G-SPEC, design-variety-scale-first 10.3).
uniqueness.source: story-library variationRules.uniqueness; design-variety-scale-first 10.3 weights; PHASE2-PLAN G-SPEC (>= 3 slots, one of them Mallow or hook, plus weighted distance >= 6.0; hook token Jaccard >= 0.5 counts as the same hook)

sequencing.$doc: Rules over the posts of one channel, in post order (story-library variationRules.sequencing). The Mallow rules apply to the unlocked set (OWNER-DECISIONS Q1 default).

cadence.$doc: Posts per channel in any 7 days. While fewer than fewMallowsBelow Mallows are unlocked, the Q1 default cap applies.
cadence.source: OWNER-DECISIONS Q1 default (Noomi-only, 3-5 posts per week per channel). 14/week is a planner default from library capacity: the valence rule needs >= 2 positive/mixed posts per 7, and the 9 positive/mixed templates hold 72 hooks under a 90-day hook cooldown, so at most 72 * 7/2 = 252 posts per 90 days (19.6/week) are possible; 21/week (design-variety-scale-first) runs out of hooks after about 2 months (docs/wp/WP-06.md)

reading.$doc: Reading-time pre-check. Every copy element is one readable text however it wraps into rows: a thought line, the whole hook (both rows), the whole end card (both rows). Each must stay on screen for at least max(min, base + perChar * characters), counting the characters of all its rows joined by a space; hook and end card use minCaption, thought lines minLine. Windows come from the beat clock of the duration. They approximate what the composer's G-DIR check measures on the real alpha curves (which are slightly shorter, because fades are not instant), so G-DIR stays the final word.

windows.hook: cyclic: (D - HOOK_IN) + HOOK_OUT, the hook returns at HOOK_IN and stays through the loop seam until HOOK_OUT (G-DIR: hook at full alpha on frame 0); first-view: 0 .. HOOK_OUT only
windows.line: L<i> .. RITUAL[0] (escalation thoughts stay until the ritual releases them)

reading.source: PHASE2-PLAN G-DIR text rules (each readable line >= max(1.0 s, 0.25 s + 0.05 s per character); hook and end line each >= 2.0 s). hookWindow 'cyclic' is a planner default (the videos loop; the cover frame is the hook at full alpha); 'first-view' is the stricter reading.

layout.$doc: Layout pre-lint with planner/metrics/fredoka-metrics.json. The estimate is multiplied by margin before it is compared (tools/font-metrics.mjs measures the model's worst error on every library string, and fails if it is above half the margin).
layout.source: story-library format.layout (hook 76 -> 50 px, 600 weight, tracking 2; resolution 62 px 500; bubble 50 px 500, padding 38 px from videos/my-brain-at-2am-v2.js bubbleCanvas); key text inside x 60-1020 (960 px), design-quality-first 8 (4% margin)

lint.$doc: Copy lint on top of templates/validate-library.mjs. Terms match whole words or phrases, case-insensitively. An entry starting with 're:' is a regular expression (case-insensitive). Topic entries (and the library's banned medical terms) are lemmas: each also matches its inflections (morphology below; FU-3), and a space or hyphen inside one matches a space, a hyphen or nothing ('self harm' -> self-harming, selfharm). An entry written '=term' matches only as written.

topics.source: story-library copyRules.general (no self-hatred, self-harm, death, illness, body/weight/food-guilt, alcohol, drugs or appearance comparisons; never catastrophic) and medicalTherapyFlags.decisionsInThisLibrary (no caffeine, dentist or 'drink water'). body-image (round 3) spells out body-image and appearance phrasing the single words miss ('I hate my body', 'I look so old', 'photoshop it out'); the library's own 'MY BODY: RESTING' and 'They look so serious.' stay legal, so 'my body' and 'look so' alone are not entries. claims (round 3): outcome promises and wellness-app framing (story-library copyRules.resolution 'never an instruction to fix, never an outcome promise'). Calibrated so every library string passes (tests/unit/planner-lint.test.mjs). FU-3: every entry is a lemma (inflections generated, planner/morph.mjs); derived words that must be refused are listed as lemmas of their own (suicidal, sickly, alcoholic, idiotic, apocalyptic); the round-4 reviewer's misses were added (suicide, heroin, cemetery, ozempic, nuclear war, margarita, ...), and a 'violence' category; 'kms', 'rip', 'weed' and 'abs' are exact ('=') because their inflections are innocent (ripped, weeding). Not one library lint verdict changed (0 of 28,935, docs/wp/FU-3.md). 'let it go' is deliberately not a song entry: it is an everyday phrase (and the ritual's own idea).

morphology.$doc: Topic entries and the library's banned medical terms are lemmas: each also matches its regular English inflections (planner/morph.mjs: -s/-es/-ies, 's, -ed/-d/-ied, -ing/-ying, -er/-est/-ier/-iest/-ers, with the e-drop, y-to-i, doubled-consonant and c-to-ck spellings), so 'smoke' refuses 'Smoked again.' and 'smokers', 'vomit' refuses 'Vomiting.', 'starve' refuses 'Starved by noon.'. Derived words (suicidal, sickly, alcoholic) are separate lemmas in the lists, never generated: derivation changes meaning (grave -> gravity). irregular adds the forms no suffix rule makes. notForms are everyday words a rule would produce from a listed lemma that are words of their own; they are never matched as inflections. An entry written '=term' is matched only as written.
morphology.source: planner default (FU-3): inflection is grammar, not a new topic, so every lemma inflects; derived and irregular words are listed by hand. 'weighted' (a weighted blanket) and 'weighting' are innocent words a rule would derive from the body-food lemma 'weight'. Calibrated: all 652 library texts still pass, and not one library lint verdict changed (docs/wp/FU-3.md).

names.$doc: A term ending in '+' also matches its English inflections (google+ matches Googled, googling, Google's; instagram+ matches Instagrammed). A space or hyphen inside a name matches a space, a hyphen or nothing, so 'coca-cola' also catches 'Coca Cola' and 'cocacola', 'tik tok+' catches 'TikTok', 'Tik-Tok' and 'tiktoks', and 'face time+' catches 'FaceTime' and 'Face Time'. Names whose split form is an everyday phrase stay glued ('iphone' not 'i phone' (I phone my mum), 'linkedin', 'powerpoint', 'bereal'). App names that are also everyday words (zoom, slack, teams, messenger, twitch, threads, outlook, excel, telegram, hinge, calm) match only in app contexts ('on Slack', 'Zoom call', 'Teams meeting', 'Hinge date', 'the Calm app'), so 'zoom in', 'cut me some slack' and 'my eye twitched' stay legal.
names.source: story-library copyRules.general (no real brands, apps, people or places by name), design-quality-first 8 (no brand, app or song names). Round 3 adds spacing variants and the names a verifier found missing (Coca Cola, Tik-Tok, Face Time, PS5, Photoshop, Wii, AirPods, Big Mac, Squishmallow and other plush brands).

lint.breathHoldSource: story-library medicalTherapyFlags (no counts, no holds, no on-screen breathing instructions; G-SINK keeps the mouth above the waterline, no underwater reading). Round 3 adds holds without a breath word (a bare 'Hold.', 'hold for a count of four', holding air or lungs, 'let the air out'), counts ('count of four'; a run of three consecutive numbers such as '2... 3... 4' is caught in code, planner/lint-copy.mjs), breathing techniques and instructions ('just breathe', 'in through the nose'). The library itself has no breath word, no hold of air and no count in any copy string, so these patterns cost it nothing ('Hold it together...' and 'Still counts.' stay legal).

breathWords.source: story-library copyRules.thought ('no breath words in the escalation (the breath belongs to the ritual)') and medicalTherapyFlags (no on-screen breathing instructions), extended by the planner to the hook and the end card (planner default): no on-screen copy names the breath, so a breathing instruction cannot hide in a phrasing the patterns above miss. The library uses no breath word in any hook or end text.

hashtags.$doc: Owner hashtags (library/brand.json) glue words together, so whole-word matching cannot see inside them (#anxietyrelief, #therapytok). Each tag is searched for every term of the library's medical and caution flags, the topics and the names, with spaces, hyphens and punctuation removed ('panic attack' -> panicattack; 're:' patterns are skipped), plus the extra terms below. A hit is excused only when a carrier word covers it: a word of the story library's own copy (all of it lint-clean, so 'still' covers 'ill') or one listed here ('pillow' covers 'pill', 'closer' covers 'loser'). The check fails closed: a new innocent tag that is flagged needs its carrier word added here, by the owner. Topic and banned medical lemmas are searched in every inflected form, glued (#suicidal is a listed derived lemma, #smoking an inflection of 'smoke'). A tag may not name a time of day either (#2am, #latenight, #bedtime; the library's literal timeWords and the timePhrases below, glued): the owner's one list goes on every video, whatever its time of day (rule time-word).
hashtags.source: design-quality-first 8 and OWNER-DECISIONS D8 (captions: library strings plus the owner-curated hashtags only); story-library copyRules.general (no brands, apps or names) and medicalTherapyFlags. 'fyp' and 'foryoupage' name TikTok's For You page. A carrier equal to a term never excuses it ('pill' is no carrier of 'pill'). The carriers here are planner defaults the owner may extend.

cautionWhitelist.reason: T13 hook[7]: 'instantly' describes the regret, not a promised outcome (the validator's only caution warning in library 1.0.0)

timeWordExemptions.reason: T02 Sunday evening: the thought is about tomorrow's alarm, so it does not set the time of day of the scene

clockTimes.$doc: Clock times the library's timeWords patterns do not spell out (2:00 AM, 2.30am, 3 a.m., TWO AM, two-thirty a.m., 2 o'clock AM, quarter to three AM, 3 in the morning, 10 at night, 02:00, 0200 hours, noon). Each explicit time maps through its hour to the ToD classes below (planner/time-words.mjs). A clock phrase is read as a whole by the planner ('two o'clock in the morning' is 2 AM): the keyword patterns (library timeWords and timePhrases below) see the text with its clock phrases blanked out, and the planner intersects their classes with the clock classes. The library validator's own reading (its timeWords on the whole text) is the floor: the planner's answer is intersected with it, so 'two o'clock in the morning' (validator: MORNING; clock: 2 AM) fits no time of day and is never planned, while '2 AM' fits late night (FU-3: copy lint stays a superset of the validator). Times without AM/PM or a part-of-day phrase (6:30, three o'clock) are ambiguous and pin nothing, as in the library. Every hour 0-23 appears exactly once.
clockTimes.source: story-library timeWords (1-4 AM, MIDNIGHT and 9-11 PM: late-night|night; 5-9 AM: morning|pre-dawn|misty-morning; 1-4 PM: afternoon|midday; 5-8 PM: golden|dusk|blue-hour|rainy-evening|night); 10-11 AM and noon are planner defaults. hm lib validate checks the shared hours against the library patterns.

timePhrases.$doc: Time words the library's timeWords do not list, matched like them (whole words or phrases, case-insensitive) and unioned with them: a text that says one of these allows only the mapped times of day. Bare day-part words that are often recollections or plans ('last night', 'this evening', 'lunch', 'breakfast') are deliberately not listed, as in the library (T01's line 'What I said at lunch.').
timePhrases.source: planner default (round 3), following the library's own classes: 'late night' sits with TONIGHT and AT NIGHT, sunrise and dawn with MORNING, sunset and dusk with SUN GOES DOWN. hm lib validate checks that every library text still fits a time of day open to its template's cast.

export.$doc: What hm export demands of <variant>/qa/report.json before it hands a final to the owner (planner/export.mjs). The report must name the exact video it judged (video.sha256 = sha256 of final.mp4) and the spec (spec.fingerprint), list at least one gate, every gate must have pass === true (false = failed, null or missing = did not run), and each required gate must be present, either by name or as sub-gates named '<gate>:<part>' (also '-', '/', '.' or a space as separator).
export.source: PHASE2-PLAN data flow step 7 (mux -> final.mp4 -> G-FINAL and G-AUDIO -> gallery -> owner decisions) and section 8 (qa/report.json: {gates: {G-SPEC..G-AUDIO: {pass, warn, metrics, artefacts}}})
